text: Consider the operations f(X,Y,Z) = X'YZ + XY' + Y'Z' and g(X,Y,Z) = X'YZ + X'YZ' + XY. Which one of the following is correct?
solution: Setting X=Y in f gives f(X,X,Z) = X'XZ + XX' + X'Z' = X'Z' = X NOR Z, and NOR is functionally complete, so {f} is functionally complete. For g, g(1,1,1) = 1 and g(0,0,0) = 0, so g preserves both 0 and 1 and by Post's criterion {g} cannot be functionally complete.
source_label: GATE Overflow question page for GATE CS 2015 Set 1 Q.39. GATE Overflow files this item under Digital Logic; the reasoning is functional completeness of a connective set
answer_evidence: So, $f$ satisfies all $5$ conditions required for functional completeness.
